chapter: Later years and the club's fate
title: Memories of the bands, Sweet Emma, and closing
summary: Happy memories of Lewis, Celestin and Robichaux, bringing Sweet Emma back, and wrapping up.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: No, it's a difficult thing, I mean, what you'd like to have and what you can afford, I guess, to see, uh, whether it's, uh, trying to run a nightclub with entertainment or, uh, buying an automobile, I guess you've got to do what you can afford to do. Of course, we tried, we tried, and we, uh, we were so happy with it. It was a wonderful sight to walk in this place and see some, uh, genuinely happy people looking up and seeing some faces on the stage, like, uh, George Lewis, Papa Selesdan, Joe Robichaud, uh, oh, name them. And incidentally, I was the first guy to put, sounds like this and there for me, first guy to put Sweet Emma back on the street. Oh, yeah. And we talked and put in the garters on and she was kind of reluctant about the garter. And the grand piano was over there in the corner and, uh, I put a little light shining on her legs so people would know where that sound was coming from, because we got tired of people asking us, who, who's playing the bells? You know, who's playing the bells? Yeah, it wouldn't be sweet, Emma.
She became quite a hit, right? Mm-hmm. Yeah. Well, I think that's about it with just about attitude.
I guess I've digressed. I didn't know exactly what you wanted to do.
Well, I can tell you about some things, I can tell you a lot about some things, and so little about some other things. Well, that's fine. That's just really about it.
